categories.name: Phone-shot · Set A
categories.summary: Kid-led reels anyone can shoot on a phone in one period. Built from outliers that hit 700K+ views at 5x+ their followers.
categories.finding: Every winner opens on a child already mid-action. No intro voiceover. The payoff is visual. 'Girls vs Boys' and 'can you name them' drive shares.

categories.name: Phone-shot · Set B
categories.summary: A second phone-shot set from a wider sweep: 1,035 reels catalogued, 24 watched. Challenge, suspense and one-take formats.
categories.finding: Lab tours and 'state-of-the-art STEM lab' montages sat at 4K to 20K views. One student, one working model, payoff on camera is what travels.

categories.name: Cinematic · Ad films
categories.summary: Ad-film concepts for the in-house crew: lens, depth of field, rack focus, high frame rate and grade planned shot by shot.
categories.finding: The cinematic reels that travelled are about one small true moment, not the school. Empty spaces with remembered voices hit 8,787x followers.

categories.name: Cinematic · Close-up films
categories.summary: Five more cinematic concepts built on macro detail, match cuts and stillness. One joins both programmes in a single student.
categories.finding: Details before faces. Sound carries half of it. 15 to 25 seconds. A presenter campus tour got 2M views and 9 shares: paid, not earned.

categories.name: Viral entertainment · Tanmay Bhat & Vir Saini formats
categories.summary: Comedy and parody films that copy the mechanism of earned viral reels: swaps, deadpan, heist, mockumentary, loop gags.
categories.finding: Tanmay Bhat's two biggest reels (137.9M, 56.1M) are paid brand collabs with almost no shares. The earned ones, like Vir Saini's 23.4M swap film, are the models here.

ideas.title: Pehli Harkat

rules: Open on a child already mid-action. No logo, no school name before the last three seconds.
Never invent a fact. Anything marked To confirm needs the school's sign-off before the shoot.
Written parental consent for every child on camera, including recorded voices.
Burn in Hinglish subtitles. Keep text out of the top 230px, bottom 480px and right 230px of a 1080x1920 frame.
Original or licensed music only, so the same cut can be boosted.
No AI-generated kids. Two high-view school reels in the research were rendered; every SBPS film is real footage.
Boost only reels that pass about 25,000 views in 72 hours (3x the account median).
